name: list_projects
title: List projects
description: The person's online KiCad projects: the ones they own and the ones shared with them, most recently changed first. Each has an id, a name, the person's role (editor or viewer), who owns it and how many documents it holds. Call this first to find the project to work on; every other tool takes the project's id or exact name.

query.description: Only projects whose name or description contains this text (case-insensitive).

name: get_project
title: Get project
description: One project: its documents (schematic sheets and the board, by path, which is what the document parameter of the other tools takes), the person's role, the members it is shared with, and the address that opens it in the web editor.

project.description: Project id or exact name, as listed by list_projects.

name: create_project
title: Create project
description: Start a new, empty online project owned by the person: a project file, one schematic sheet and one board, named after the project. Returns its id and documents. Use it only when the person asks for a new project or design.

name: get_design_guide
title: Design guide
description: House rules for working on a design here, written for you: how to draw a schematic that reads like a careful engineer's, how to take a design from a prompt to a routed board in stages, how to plan placement and routing for the engines, and how to review a design. Read the relevant topic once before you draw or rearrange a schematic, lay out or route a board, or write a review.

topic.description: Which part to read; all when omitted.

name: render_view
title: Render image
description: A picture of a schematic sheet or of the board as it is right now, drawn the way the editor draws it (KiCad's colours and stroke font). Use it to see layout, readability and placement that lists of coordinates do not show, and to check your own changes after applying them. Without area or refs it shows the whole sheet or board; a schematic sheet is large, so ask for the part you care about to be able to read values and pin names.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

area.description: The rectangle to show, [x0, y0, x1, y1] in millimetres.

refs.description: Show these components and their surroundings instead of an area.

layers.description: Board only: draw just these layers, for example ["F.Cu", "Edge.Cuts"]. Default: every layer the editor shows by default.

width_px.description: Longest side of the image in pixels (default 1500).

name: read_document
title: Read source
description: A document as KiCad s-expression text, as it stands now: the file's header followed by every item. For reading exact syntax (to write an add_item edit that matches the file, or to inspect something no structured tool reports). Long documents come in parts; pass next_offset back as offset. Prefer list_components, list_nets and get_items for questions about the design, they are far shorter.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

name: list_changes
title: List changes
description: The changes made to a project through this connection or the person's other connected apps, newest first: an id, the title, what each edit did, the document, when, and whether it has been undone. The id is what undo_changes and redo_changes take.

name: undo_changes
title: Undo a change
description: Take back one apply_changes call: what it added is removed, what it removed comes back, what it moved or edited returns to how it was, and board rules it set are restored. Everyone in the document sees it happen. It is refused, with nothing changed, when somebody has edited one of the same items since, so nobody's newer work is overwritten. Undo the newest change first when undoing several.

change_id.description: The change to undo, as returned by apply_changes or list_changes. Omit for the most recent change to the project that has not been undone.

name: redo_changes
title: Redo a change
description: Put back a change that undo_changes took away, exactly as it was applied (the same items with the same ids, and the board rules it set). Like an undo it is refused, with nothing changed, when somebody has edited one of the same items since.

change_id.description: The undone change to put back, from list_changes. Omit for the change that was undone most recently.

name: list_comments
title: List comments
description: The review comments people have pinned on a schematic sheet or the board: each thread with what it is pinned to (on: a component or item, net: a net), its position in millimetres, author, text, replies and whether it is resolved. Resolved threads are left out unless include_resolved is true.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

name: add_comment
title: Add comment
description: Pin a comment on a schematic sheet or the board, signed as the person, where everyone in the project sees it: on a component (ref), on a net (net), or at a point (x, y in millimetres). A comment on a component follows the component when it is moved; one on a net highlights the net when opened. Or answer an existing thread with reply_to. Good for review findings the person wants left on the design; do not comment unless asked to.

document.description: Document path as listed by get_project, or "board".

net.description: Pin it on this net, by the name list_nets gives.

reply_to.description: The id of the thread to reply to, from list_comments.

name: resolve_comment
title: Resolve comment
description: Mark a comment thread resolved once what it asked for is done, or reopen it with resolved false.

name: list_checkpoints
title: List checkpoints
description: The named checkpoints of a project (the versions people saved under a name), newest first, with the documents each covers.

name: create_checkpoint
title: Create checkpoint
description: Save a named checkpoint of the project, the way File > Save Checkpoint does in the editor, so the person can find this state in the project's history. A project linked to GitHub with checkpoint pushes turned on pushes it there as well.

name.description: A short name, for example "Before rerouting the USB pair".
